author: Ethan Goode
title: Incumbent DA Hillar Moore faces challenger Ryan Thompson in November election - NewsBreak
text:
By Ethan Goode ,
10 hours ago
BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — With Election Day approaching, voters in East Baton Rouge Parish will soon decide who will lead the District Attorney’s Office, as longtime incumbent Hillar Moore III faces a challenge from public defender Ryan Thompson.
Both candidates say public safety is a top priority, but they bring different professional backgrounds and approaches to addressing crime, accountability, and the future of the criminal justice system.
Thompson, a Democrat, is campaigning on a platform centered around equal justice, transparency, accountability and addressing the underlying causes of crime.
A graduate of Southern University Law Center, Thompson has spent nearly a decade working in the East Baton Rouge Office of the Public Defender, where he rose through the ranks from investigator to felony assistant and section chief.
“I’ve been a public defender for almost a decade. I started working at an office as an investigator, and then I went from an investigator to a felony assistant,” Thompson said.
Thompson said his experience working with people involved in the criminal justice system has shaped his approach to public safety.
His campaign emphasizes prioritizing violent crime prosecutions while also connecting individuals with mental health services and other community resources.
Thompson has also focused on grassroots campaigning, going door-to-door to connect with residents and hear their concerns about crime and the justice system.
Moore has served as East Baton Rouge Parish District Attorney since 2009 and is seeking to continue his leadership of the office.
Before becoming district attorney, Moore worked as an FBI-trained crime scene investigator. He earned his bachelor’s degree in criminal justice from Louisiana State University and his law degree from Southern University Law Center.
During his tenure, Moore’s office has implemented several initiatives aimed at reducing violence, supporting crime victims and improving court operations.
Those efforts include the Stop the Loss and TRUCE violence-reduction programs, an expanded Victim’s Assistance Program and the Baton Rouge Easy Expungement Screening program.
Moore’s office also introduced a 72-hour arraignment process intended to help move criminal cases through the court system more efficiently.
“I want to make sure that I leave this office in a really good position, not only financially, but also with steady employees, assistant district attorneys, investigators, victims counselors,” Moore said.
Looking ahead, Moore says education and early intervention should play a larger role in preventing crime.
“Crime is directly related to education or the lack of education,” Moore said, emphasizing the importance of addressing truancy and investing in early childhood education.
While Thompson is campaigning on bringing a different perspective to the District Attorney’s Office, Moore is highlighting his experience, existing programs and plans for the future.
Both candidates have identified violent crime and community safety as major concerns facing East Baton Rouge Parish.
Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Polls in Louisiana will be open from 6 a.m. until 8 p.m.
